page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at top centre with the page number at top left. No marginal notes. Catchword-like line "I. DEI" at the lower right, below the last line.

main_text.p: scripsi, quia nonnihil facit ad intelligendum Pauli Apostoli dictum, 1.Cor.14.20. Fratres, ne estote pueri intelligentia: sed malitia pueri, intelligentia vero adulti estote. Interdum tamen κακίαν ἀντὶ τῆς κα-κώσεως[?] fumi, ex illo Christi dicto liquet: Sufficit diei sua uexatio, ἡ κακία[?]. Matt.6. 34. Exiftimo tamen, malitiam in uerbis Ionae uniuersaliter sumtam pro impietate & iniusticia, id est, de horrenda & multiplici transgressione primae & secundae tabulae Decalogi.

4. Malitia cur coram Domino ascendere dicatur. Nubi ascendenti confertur peccatu, Isa.44.22. Deleui ut nubem praeuaricationes tuas, & ueluti nubem peccata tua: redi igitur ad me, quia redemi te. Vt enim densa & caliginosa nubes, Solis fulgorem nobis eripiens, tenebras inducit: ita quoque peccata intermedia obstant, ne serenam Dei faciem aspicere peccatores queant, neue lucis diuinae radijs eorum corda illustrentur.
¶ Iam uero ut ad θεὸν[?] progrediamur, duae nobis occurrunt: altera de uocatione, altera de poenitentia.

page.notes: The Greek words in the first paragraph ("κακίαν ἀντὶ τῆς κακώσεως" and "ἡ κακία") are hard to read on the scan and may be misprinted or misread; they are marked [?]. The Greek after "ad" is also uncertain. The "I. DEI" line at the foot is treated as a catchword; it could be a signature or other furniture. The "Matt.6. 34." reference is split across the line end and is kept in the same paragraph as printed. The first line "scripsi," is a continuation from the previous page.
